# Data Reproducibility

In this document you gonna learn how to reproduce data of glowworm and make your changes to get final and polished dataset.


first you need to load required packages and function all together in one file `vignette-utils.R` and import them with `source()` in R. In order to make change in functions you can access this utile file in this address: `ecotourism/vignettes/vignette-utils.R`

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
source("vignette-utils.R")
```

We are investigating occurrence data of [**Glowworms**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glowworm) in Australia from the **Atlas of Living Australia**, and make a map showing the spatial locations of sightings from 2014 to 2024. so at the beginning we want to define global variables that using in for function inputs.

```{r echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
# global variables
email <- "vahdatjavad@gmail.com"
organism_name <- "glowworms"
organism_title <- "Glowworms"
taxa     <- "Arachnocampa"
start    <- 2014
end      <- 2024
```

With the function of `obs_data` you can connect to occurrence data from ALA for a given taxon and time range and also you need to sign up with your email address in ALA website first. We are passing Retrieved data to `polished_data()` function in order to change some column name and also filter `NA` and missing data. Because it is a general function (that means you can change just taxa name and receive new dataset.) so that we use general name for assigning data but in the next section you can see that this dataset will be saved with `organism_name` in `/data` folder. 

```{r eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
organism <- obs_data(taxa, start, end, your_email=email) |> polished_data()
```

After receiving data from ALA we want to save it in R data format `rda` because it is compressed format and good to save our dataset in R data format. function of `mysave()` written by myself to automatically save `organism` dataset with `organism_name` in `/data` format. 

```{r eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
mysave(organism_name, organism)
```


Now we want to add nearest `weather station` to each occurance of data. With `attach_nearest_station()` function we adding new column with name `weather_station_id` to data set and then save it again. 

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
attach_nearest_station(organism_name)
```


Because providing 10 years daily weather data for all stations are very hug and heavy data set, so we just chose top 3 station for each organism and then retrieved weather data just for those 3 station. 

So your final data looks like this:

```{r, echo=TRUE}
load("../data/glowworms.rda")
glimpse(glowworms)
```

# Data Analysis 

You learned how to find your data and request to download from galah api. here is more detail for ```r organism_title```. Below we are going to be more detailed in our organism.  


## Saving raw data set for furtur analysis

Because we want to do more changes in our dataset and do not want to change main dataset so we will download our primarily data set to ```organism_raw``` and save it in ```data_raw``` folder. 

```{r "request data ALA", eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

organism_raw <- obs_data(taxa, start, end) |> polished_data()
# Save data
mysave_raw(organism_name, organism_raw)
```

The function `mysave_raw()` is the user defined function and you can access it from `ecotourism/vignettes/vignette-utils.R` it will save your data with real organism name directly in `data_raw/` folder with ```r paste0(organism_name,"_raw.rda")```

This is the head of data set:

```{r "print head of data", echo=FALSE}
organism_raw <- myload_raw(organism_name)
organism_raw |> slice_head(n = 3) |> as_tibble() |> glimpse()
```

Now we want to know the number of occurrence in each state:

```{r "number of occ in state", echo=FALSE}
organism_raw |> my_count(scientificName, obs_state) |> as_tibble() 
```

This is the selected species and in the next we will consider all `Arachnocampa` around `Arachnocampa flava` as a `falava` because `Arachnocampa` is a genus species.

```{r echo=TRUE, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}

# Clean and prepare data
organism_raw |> 
  filter(!is.na(obs_lat), !is.na(obs_lon), !is.na(month), 
         scientificName == "Arachnocampa" | 
         scientificName == "Arachnocampa flava" |
         scientificName == "Arachnocampa tasmaniensis") |> 
  plot_map1(color_by = scientificName)

```

we want to assign genus "Arachnocampa" records to the "Arachnocampa flava" specie — based on how close they are geographically to other records (250 Kilometers radius).

```{r echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# Set radius threshold in meters (250 km)
radius_threshold <- 250000

# Split into unknowns and references
unknowns <- organism_raw |> 
  filter(scientificName == "Arachnocampa")

references <- organism_raw |> 
  filter(scientificName == "Arachnocampa flava")

# Function to assign if within distance
assign_if_close_to_flava <- function(lat, lon, flava_data, radius) {
  dists <- distHaversine(
    matrix(c(lon, lat), ncol = 2),
    matrix(c(flava_data$obs_lon, flava_data$obs_lat), ncol = 2)
  )
  if (any(dists <= radius)) {
    return("Arachnocampa flava")
  } else {
    return("Arachnocampa")  # Keep unchanged
  }
}

# Apply to unknowns
unknowns_updated <- unknowns |> 
  rowwise() |> 
  mutate(scientificName = assign_if_close_to_flava(obs_lat, obs_lon, references, radius_threshold)) |> 
  ungroup()


# Combine with other records
organism <- organism_raw |> 
  filter(scientificName != "Arachnocampa") |> 
  bind_rows(unknowns_updated) |> 
  filter(!is.na(obs_lat), !is.na(obs_lon), !is.na(month), 
         scientificName == "Arachnocampa flava" |
         scientificName == "Arachnocampa tasmaniensis")

  
mysave(organism_name, organism)
```

## Nearest Weather Station Mapping 

Here we want to know for each occurrence of data which weather station is close so that we can use `attach_nearest_station()` function and add new column `weather_station_id` represent nearest weather station to this record.

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
attach_nearest_station(organism_name)
```

```{r eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
organism <- myload(organism_name)

head(organism, n = 2) |> as_tibble() |> glimpse()
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}

summarize_state_frequencies(organism_name)

```

Interpretation:

-    Queensland:\
    61 of your organism records were observed in Queensland.\
    However, only 17 of those were linked to weather stations also located in Queensland.

-   Tasmania:\
    40 observations were made in Tasmania, and\
    All 40 were matched to Tasmanian weather stations — a perfect match.

-   New South Wales:\
    23 observations occurred there,\
    But 67 records were linked to weather stations in New South Wales — suggesting many observations from other states were matched to NSW stations.
